quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.

questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle so you have time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: What causes "highway hypnosis"?

options.text: Staring at the road ahead for a long time without looking around.
Getting too much sleep the night before.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road ahead for a long time without looking around.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead without looking side to side or behind you. This causes you to zone out and may lead to crashes with vehicles that slow down or stop in front of you.

questions.question: Which statement about speed is correct?

options.text: Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.
Speeding is safe if you are a good driver.
Both driving too slowly on some highways and speeding can be dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both driving too slowly on some highways and speeding can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the more likely a crash will be fatal. At speeds over 80 miles per hour, survival in a crash is very unlikely. Driving slower than other traffic is also dangerous because other drivers may make risky moves to pass you.

questions.question: How can you avoid crashes caused by drinking and driving?

options.text: Decide before you drink that you will not drive.
Say no if someone offers you a drink because you are driving.

questions.explanation: Decide before drinking that you will not drive. Alcohol affects your judgment, so it becomes harder to make safe choices after you start drinking.

questions.question: When turning, you must ____ your speed.
questions.explanation: When turning, slow down to a speed that lets you control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and respond to surprises.

questions.question: What must a driver do when dealing with pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give the pedestrian the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
Only give the right-of-way when the pedestrian has the legal right to cross.
Slow down and honk your horn near a crosswalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give the pedestrian the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
questions.explanation: Do everything you can to avoid hitting a pedestrian or another vehicle. You must always let pedestrians cross first, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually ____ and must always be obeyed.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs control how traffic moves. They are usually white with black markings and drivers must always follow them.

questions.question: What do downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to do?
questions.explanation: Downward-facing triangular signs tell drivers to yield. When it is safe and the road is clear, you may then proceed.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: Give the right-of-way to any emergency vehicle using a siren or flashing lights.

questions.question: At night, what is hardest to see?
questions.explanation: At night, people walking are harder to see than road signs and other objects.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.

questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting an expressway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, or when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: You are stopped at a stop sign in a line of vehicles. Other vehicles ahead have passed through with no cross traffic. What should you do?

options.text: You may go through the intersection without stopping again.
You must stop at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.
You may slowly roll past the stop sign.
You may follow the vehicle ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.
questions.explanation: Always bring your vehicle to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip your stop just because other vehicles have already gone through.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: A road joins from the right.
The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road ahead turns sharply right, then sharply left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead turns sharply to the right and then sharply to the left.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are in:
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be extra careful on roads shaded by trees or buildings. These areas freeze faster than other parts of the road and take longer to dry.

questions.question: What do speed limit signs tell you?

options.text: Possible driving speeds for the area.
The highest or lowest legal speed allowed on that road.
The speed to drive in heavy traffic.
The speed to drive in poor conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The highest or lowest legal speed allowed on that road.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs show the maximum or minimum safe speed allowed. The maximum speed is for ideal conditions. You must slow down when weather or road conditions require it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash means that action is not allowed. Right turns are prohibited where this sign is posted.

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
Honk your horn to warn them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in someone else's blind spot. Move forward or backward so the other driver can see your vehicle.

questions.question: Vehicle stopping distance does NOT depend on:

options.text: Your vehicle's tire condition and type.

questions.explanation: Stopping distance depends on your reaction time, weather and visibility, vehicle weight, brake condition, tire condition and type, road conditions, and speed. Time of day does not affect stopping distance.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Turn the wheel hard in the opposite direction.
Turn your steering wheel toward traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear is sliding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear is sliding.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle skids, stay calm. Steer in the same direction the skid is moving.

questions.question: This sign shows:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that an intersection with a crossing road is ahead.

questions.question: When changing lanes to the left, where should you look to check your blind spot?
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot, look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.

questions.question: What does alcohol do to your driving ability?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain activity and reduces your driving skills. It makes your reflexes slower and your judgment worse.

questions.question: Traffic moving in opposite directions is divided by ____ lines.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions.

questions.question: After a school bus stops to let children out, what should you do?

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you.
Watch for children walking along the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road.
questions.explanation: After a school bus stops with its lights flashing, watch for children walking along the side of the road. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: What is defensive driving?

options.text: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to prevent accidents.
Passing poor drivers to get ahead in traffic.
Following the car ahead very closely.
Quickly changing lanes to avoid traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Spotting dangerous situations and taking action to prevent accidents.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means you notice dangerous situations before they happen and take action to avoid accidents. It helps you stay safe around all types of drivers.
